name: Iva

project_scope.selection_mode: Approved Master Plant Pool pair, both represented by canonical learner cards; genus lesson only
project_scope.source_pool: Hays_Botany_ID_Master_Curation_Tracker > Master Plant Pool, rows 590–591; Genus Study Index row 118

accepted_name_mapping.canonical_name: Iva asperifolia var. angustifolia (Nutt. ex DC.) B.L.Turner
accepted_name_mapping.relationship: homotypic synonym / accepted variety under POWO; FNA key uses older Iva angustifolia name
accepted_name_mapping.instruction: Search and compare under both names; never create an independent duplicate Iva angustifolia card.

shared_genus_recognition.look_here_first: Start with mature mid-stem leaves: measure petiole length and blade width, check the entire versus toothed edge, then examine a mature head's involucre and outer phyllary seams. Photograph lower and upper nodes to learn opposite-to-alternate phyllotaxy; leaf arrangement alone does not distinguish the two taxa.
shared_traits: Annual herbs in this study pair with simple rough, gland-dotted leaves; lower stem leaves can be opposite and upper leaves alternate. Check multiple nodes before describing leaf arrangement.
Small rayless (discoid-looking) capitula borne in roughly spike-like arrays; each head has an involucre, receptacular paleae, and separate functionally pistillate and staminate florets.
Dry one-seeded cypselas develop after flowering; examine the whole head and florets with magnification to confirm Asteraceae.
shared_genus_recognition.false_friend: A spike-like display is an array of multiple capitula, not one grass spike or one long ordinary flower.

species_comparison_matrix.Iva annua: Evidently petiolate: usually 5–20 mm, sometimes to 30 mm

species_comparison_matrix.Iva angustifolia: Lance-linear to linear, usually 12–25 mm long × 1–4 mm wide (extremes longer/wider); margins entire
species_comparison_matrix.Iva annua: Usually broadly deltate/ovate through lanceolate, typically 30–100 mm long × 8–45 mm wide (sometimes much larger); margins toothed

species_comparison_matrix.Iva angustifolia: Approximately prismatic-top-shaped (turbinate), 2.5–3 mm; outer 3–5 phyllaries partly united (connate)
species_comparison_matrix.Iva annua: Approximately hemispheric, 3–4(–5) mm; outer 3–5 phyllaries separate (distinct)

species_comparison_matrix.Iva angustifolia: Often 20–60 cm, occasionally over 100 cm; flowering commonly Sep–Nov
species_comparison_matrix.Iva annua: Often 50–100 cm, occasionally over 150 cm; flowering commonly Jul–Nov

species_comparison_matrix.Iva angustifolia: Opposite lower leaves, often alternate above (accepted learner concept: I. asperifolia var. angustifolia)
species_comparison_matrix.Iva annua: Lower leaves generally opposite; upper leaves may be alternate
species_comparison_matrix.weight: SHARED/NOT DIAGNOSTIC: compare several lower and upper nodes; prioritize petiole, margin and phyllary characters

look_here_first_sequence.inspect: a mature mid-stem leaf at its stem attachment
look_here_first_sequence.decision: Very narrow entire blade + petiole 0–2 mm favors I. angustifolia; wider toothed blade + petiole usually 5–20 mm favors I. annua. Also record opposite lower versus alternate upper leaf nodes as a shared teaching feature, not a species tie-breaker.

look_here_first_sequence.inspect: several intact rayless heads from a mature inflorescence
look_here_first_sequence.decision: Turbinate involucre and partly fused outer phyllaries favor I. angustifolia; hemispheric involucre and free outer phyllaries favor I. annua.
Count functionally pistillate and staminate florets to support (not replace) leaf and involucre evidence.
Retain Iva sp. and request a measured leaf/node plus intact heads; do not force a species determination.

scientific_cautions: Do not treat number of florets as an absolute binary key: Flora of North America uses open-ended counts, especially for I. angustifolia.
Both grow in disturbed and often moist sites; habitat cannot replace leaf/involucre anatomy.

Both source-pool names are represented in the current canonical manifest: Iva annua and Iva asperifolia var. angustifolia (source-pool Iva angustifolia is a synonym). No new species install is needed.

Flora of North America uses Iva angustifolia, whereas the canonical learner uses accepted Iva asperifolia var. angustifolia (POWO); retain synonym search and do not create a duplicate. Historical I. texensis usage requires separate taxonomic review, not an automatic alias decision.
I. annua's leaf outline is variable; prioritize the combination of petiole length, teeth, and phyllary union.
No native-range PASS or county certification is made by this genus lesson.
Both taxa may show opposite lower leaves and alternate upper leaves; do not teach 'all leaves alternate' as a genus diagnosis or a species separator. Photograph a sequence of nodes.

local_lookalike_routing.test: Check sex-specific flower-head architecture: often distinct staminate heads and separate pistillate burr-forming structures; compare fruiting involucres and leaves rather than assuming every green spike is Iva.

local_lookalike_routing.taxon: Cyclachaena xanthifolia (encounter comparison; verify local occurrence)
local_lookalike_routing.test: Large triangular toothed leaves can resemble I. annua; verify broad, branched panicle arrangement and fruiting heads rather than a leaf-only ID.
Woody or shrubby stems with separate male/female plants and differently structured discoid heads/pappus; compare head sex and cypsela/pappus, not just rayless appearance.
Confirm involucre profile, outer phyllary union, leaf petiole/margin, and actual floret arrangement under magnification.

diagnostic_photo_requirements.role: matched mature leaf with node and ruler
diagnostic_photo_requirements.show: leaf shape, entire vs toothed margins, 0–2 mm vs 5–20 mm petiole, labels on same-scale pair
turbinate vs hemispheric involucre; millimeter ruler; arrow to each outer phyllary
partly connate vs free outer 3–5 phyllaries, same orientation; avoid obscuring fusion line
receptacle, paleae, functionally pistillate and staminate florets separately labeled; count multiple heads
multiple tiny capitula distributed in spike-like arrays, not a single flower
mature cypselas plus involucre; label sample as reference, not definitive species split

dependencies.detail: Both accepted learner concepts are already canonical; do not reinstall. Preserve source-pool Iva angustifolia as an alias to the existing variety, and route any unresolved I. texensis identity question to taxonomy review.

anatomy_lessons.title: 1 · Measure the petiole at the node
anatomy_lessons.plain_language: The little stalk between the stem and leaf blade
anatomy_lessons.look_for: Measure several fully expanded mid-stem leaves at their stem attachment: 0–2 mm in I. angustifolia versus usually 5–20 mm in I. annua. Include a ruler and full leaf margin; small immature leaves can mislead. Record whether lower leaves are opposite and upper leaves alternate; this is a shared pattern, not the species split.
anatomy_lessons.why_it_matters: The combination of leaf stalk, blade width and entire versus toothed edge is the first useful field split.
anatomy_lessons.photo_role: matched exact-species node + full leaf + millimeter scale
anatomy_lessons.photo_status: Existing four species gallery files confirmed on main; none certified to demonstrate petiole measurements or node phyllotaxy; paired scale photos needed.

anatomy_lessons.title: 2 · Turn the head sideways
anatomy_lessons.plain_language: A tiny flower head and the green wrapper beneath it
anatomy_lessons.look_for: Each spike-like branch holds multiple separate rayless capitula. Compare the narrow top-shaped ~2.5–3 mm involucre of I. angustifolia with the rounded ~3–5 mm involucre of I. annua, measuring intact mature heads.
anatomy_lessons.why_it_matters: These are composite heads, not a single spike flower; head profile can corroborate the leaf characters.
anatomy_lessons.photo_role: matched lateral head macros, same magnification, ruler in plane
anatomy_lessons.photo_status: needed; external references do not count as installed

anatomy_lessons.title: 3 · Find the outer phyllary seams
anatomy_lessons.plain_language: Green bracts under the head, either joined at the base or separate
anatomy_lessons.look_for: Under a hand lens examine outer 3–5 phyllaries: partly fused (connate) in I. angustifolia, distinct in I. annua. Photograph the actual seams in the same orientation; do not infer fusion from a distant flowering-axis view.
anatomy_lessons.why_it_matters: Phyllary fusion is a more decisive reproductive tie-breaker than head color.
anatomy_lessons.photo_role: side and underside macro showing the base of outer phyllaries

anatomy_lessons.title: 4 · Dissect one rayless head
anatomy_lessons.plain_language: Separate seed-forming and pollen-forming little flowers inside one head
anatomy_lessons.look_for: Separate the outer functionally pistillate florets from inner staminate florets and receptacular paleae. Count several mature heads: counts overlap and should support, not replace, leaf/petiole/phyllary evidence.
anatomy_lessons.why_it_matters: Explains why a rayless Asteraceae head is still made of many individual florets.
anatomy_lessons.photo_role: dissected head with separately labeled florets and mm scale

comparison_cards.title: Narrowleaf marsh-elder versus sumpweed
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Measure mid-stem petioles and check entire narrow versus toothed broader leaves; confirm phyllary fusion on mature heads.
comparison_cards.caution: Leaf sizes, plant heights and floret counts vary; never force an ID from a single young leaf.
comparison_cards.status: Both canonical learner concepts installed; comparison anatomy remains provisional and unannotated.

comparison_cards.title: Iva versus ragweed
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Check whether heads are arranged as Iva rayless capitula versus ragweed's separate pollen-producing and fruiting structures; inspect mature fruiting heads.
comparison_cards.caution: A green spike-like flowering display and rough leaves alone are not diagnostic; confirm with reproductive anatomy.
comparison_cards.status: comparison only; no occurrence or native-range claim

comparison_cards.title: Iva versus other rayless composites
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Check herbaceous versus woody habit, head sex and branching, involucre/phyllaries, and pappus; use exact local specimen references.
comparison_cards.caution: Comparison genera are visual look-alikes, not newly installed Iva species or confirmed local records.
